correctness.rationale: For J=diag(1,−1), KJ+JK=2aJ, so the unique stable periodic covariance is T₀K⁻¹+q(t)J where q′=−2aq+2δσ. Half-period antisymmetry fixes q(0)=−(δ/a)tanh(aτ). Integration of q(t)² on the positive half-period gives (δ/a)²[1−tanh(aτ)/(aτ)]; its mean over both halves is zero. The globally randomized phase gives time translation invariance. Conditional future increments have mean zero, so the covariance at lag h≥0 is e^(−Kh) times the averaged one-time covariance, and the opposite lag is its transpose. The covariance of the conditional variances is −E[q²], whereas the off-diagonal covariance is the constant −kT₀/(a²−k²); conditional Wick pairing thus adds exactly twice its square. The marginal fourth cumulants are 3E[q²], and the mixed one is −E[q²]. F increases strictly from 0 to 1 because the numerator of F′ has derivative 2z sech²(z)tanh(z). Thus for k≠0 a finite crossing requires R>√2u/(1−u²), and some R<1 meets this precisely when 0<u<√(2−√3). Equality in the contrast condition gives a zero only at infinite half-period; k=0 is strictly negative at every positive half-period. The illustrative parameters give target 128/729 as stated.
residual_risks: The all-lag equality is an equality of second moments, not full time-series laws. The fourth cumulants use the global uniform-phase mixture; fixed-phase marginals are Gaussian.
Equal diagonals are used for the exact fourth-order formula; they are not a necessary condition for the general covariance-averaging identity with constant K and isotropic average noise.

value.rationale: In a natural symmetric thermal model even the whole second-order stationary time series fails to distinguish the switched baths from equilibrium. Negative squared-coordinate covariance is impossible for a centered Gaussian pair, and this result says exactly when it is visible and when no permissible contrast yields a crossing. It supplies a diagnostic regime and a sharp limit on it, rather than merely the existence of non-Gaussian phase mixtures.
residual_risks: The squared-coordinate covariance is not a heat-current or entropy-production law and no finite-sample detection guarantee is established.
